title: Adaptive access recertification driven by residency and risk signals
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an adaptive access recertification system that schedules periodic reviews and just-in-time certification tasks based on tenant data residency changes and risk signals (login anomalies, privileged role changes, third-party token grants). The goal is to reduce reviewer fatigue by prioritizing high-risk, high-residency-impact accounts and automating evidence bundle generation for auditors.
acceptance_criteria: System ingests residency change events and maps them to tenant recert windows (e.g., EU-resident tenants get quarterly recert prompts).
Risk scoring pipeline tags identities with low/medium/high and influences recert cadence and reviewer assignment.
Automated evidence bundles (user entitlements, recent SSO/SCIM events, last activity timestamps) can be exported per-review in ZIP/JSONL format and uploaded to the compliance S3 bucket.
Reviewer workflow surfaces prioritized queue in Console with ability to approve/revoke and annotate; actions generate audit entries and SCIM deprovision templates when revocation occurs.
End-to-end tests validate that residency flips (region relocation) trigger an expedited recert task within 24 hours and that the task is marked high priority.
System operates within privacy constraints and does not export PII in evidence bundles; security review sign-off obtained before rollout.
tasks: Design risk scoring model and map signals (auth anomalies, new admin grants, recent token rotations)
Event bridge: residency-change -> recert orchestration lambda
Create reviewer queue UI in Console with filters (tenant region, risk, last recert date)
Implement evidence bundle generator; redact PII and sign with KMS before upload
SCIM action templates for bulk revocation and suggested remediation steps
E2E test harness: simulate residency change and validate evidence artifact and audit entries
Run security review and include findings in rollout plan
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with PM and Compliance; scoped required signals and agreed S3 artifact spec (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMP/Adaptive+Recert+Spec)

2025-02-28: Console wireframes reviewed by Design; request to add bulk-approve and comment templates (Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/recert-queue)
2025-03-05: Evidence generator MVP committed; KMS integration stubbed, awaiting security review ticket (SEC-2101)
2025-03-12: Integration tests green for residency event -> recert task creation; next: redact/PII validation and reviewer UX polish
notes: Design decision: use short-lived presigned links for evidence bundle downloads to minimize exposure.
Trade-off: aggressive redaction reduces auditor convenience; plan to provide field-level metadata to assist reviewers.
Follow-up: schedule a pilot with two mid-market customers in EU region to validate cadence assumptions.
